easy.def: To leave a place because of danger.
examples: We evacuated the building.
The people evacuated the town.
Everyone evacuated.

more.def: To leave a place quickly because it is not safe.
examples: The school evacuated when the fire alarm rang.
The town was evacuated before the flood.
Everyone evacuated the building calmly.

easy.def: Used to show something is surprising.
examples: Even the baby laughed.
It is even bigger than me.
She did not even cry.

more.def: Used to stress that something is more than you might think.
examples: Even the tallest kid could not reach the top shelf.
The day was cold, and it was even colder at night.
He was so tired that he could not even stand.
The floor is even.
An even road is easy to ride on.
The table is not even.

more.def: Flat and level, or the same in amount or size.
examples: The path across the field was smooth and even.
The two teams were even at halftime, with five points each.
Cut the cake into even pieces so everyone gets the same.

easy.def: The time at the end of the day.
examples: We eat dinner in the evening.
It is cool in the evening.
Good evening, everyone!

more.def: The part of the day between afternoon and night.
examples: In the evening, the owls start to hoot.
We watched the sunset on a warm summer evening.
My family takes a walk every evening.
The party was a fun event.
The big event is today.
The picnic is a school event.

more.def: Something that happens, especially something important or planned.
examples: The school fair is the biggest event of the year.
A storm was the main event of the week.
The swimming event starts at noon.
Eventually, the rain stopped.
The seed will eventually grow.
He eventually fell asleep.

more.def: At last, after a long time or many steps.
examples: Eventually, the snow melted and the grass grew.
After many tries, she eventually learned to ride the bike.
The bus was late, but it eventually arrived.
Have you ever swum?
Did you ever see a whale?
It is the best cake ever.

more.def: At any time, or at all times.
examples: Have you ever seen a shooting star?
This was the biggest fish he had ever caught.
The tree has been growing ever since I was a baby.
I brush my teeth every day.
Every kid got a prize.
She knows every word.

more.def: Each one of a group, with none left out, or each time something happens.
examples: Every student in the class got a turn on the swing.
We visit my grandmother every Sunday.
He cleaned every corner of the room.
Everybody is here.
Everybody sang.
Hello, everybody!
Everybody in the class got a turn on the swing.
The teacher asked everybody to line up at the door.
Everybody cheered when the team scored.
I wear everyday clothes.
This is an everyday plate.
It is an everyday job.

more.def: Ordinary and used or seen on any normal day.
examples: I wear everyday shoes to school.
Cooking is an everyday task.
The everyday dishes are in the cupboard.
Everyone is here.
Hello, everyone!
Everyone clapped.
Everyone in the class brought a snack to share.
The teacher waited until everyone was quiet.
Everyone cheered when the team won.
I packed everything.
Everything is ready.
She knows everything.

more.def: All things, or each thing in a group.
examples: We packed everything into the car before the trip.
Everything in the room was covered with dust.
The kitten wants to explore everything.
Toys are everywhere.
I looked everywhere.
Leaves were everywhere.
Snow covered everything everywhere.
I searched everywhere for my hat.
Bees were buzzing everywhere in the garden.

easy.def: Facts that show something is true.
examples: Footprints are evidence that a deer came by.
The clues were evidence.
We found evidence of a fox.

more.def: Facts or signs that show that something is true.
examples: Muddy footprints were evidence that someone had come in.
Scientists look for evidence before they decide.
The nibbled leaves were evidence of a rabbit.
The evil witch cast a spell.
The evil king was mean.
It was an evil plan.

more.def: Very bad and cruel, and wishing to hurt others.
examples: The evil queen in the fairy tale was cruel to everyone.
The hero stopped the evil plan.
In the story, an evil wizard cast a spell.

easy.def: Slow change over a long time.
examples: The evolution of animals took long.
The evolution of the bike.
Evolution is slow.

more.def: The slow change of living things over millions of years, or any slow development.
examples: The evolution of birds took millions of years.
The evolution of the telephone is interesting.
Scientists study evolution.

easy.def: To change slowly over a long time.
examples: Animals evolve.
The plant evolved.
The story evolved.

more.def: To change and develop slowly over a very long time.
examples: Animals evolve over millions of years.
The game evolved as people added new rules.
The small town evolved into a big city.
